newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares make up some Dow-inspired losses.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares make up some Dow-inspired losses.

text.p: Leading Russian shares recovered some losses on Wednesday triggered by the Dow Jones' first close under 8,000 in three weeks and were seen finishing near Tuesday levels as Russia consolidated recent gains, traders said.
They saw the market rising next week on increased fund flows.

"The market feels like it is consolidating," said Brunswick's Martin Diggle, predicting shares would rise or fall by up to five percent for a week or so before climbing again. "It believes there will be new inflows in September."
The Russian Trading System 21-share index opened slightly off its previous close at 557.64 after 557.99. It has been climbing fairly steadily since late April when it was under 300.
A trend line joining market highs in May and early July suggested technical resistance would emerge towards 590. A parallel trend line touching the low in mid-June pointed to chart support near 510.
LUKoil oil producer had recovered to $27.15 at 0845 GMT on the Russian Trading System from $26.90 in the first fifteen minutes of trade but off $27.36 at the previous close.
Rye, Man and Gor Securities trader Igor Kozhechkin said higher liquidity was helping shares listed on Monday on the RTS.
A number of shares listed on the RTS on Monday showed strong gains and movement. Manufacturer Kirovsky Zavod opened at $18.25 after $17.40 on Tuesday.

He said foreign markets' performance had hit Russia in the morning -- the Dow Jones index fell below 8,000 for the first time in three weeks to close unofficially at 7961. But Russian shares would probably find support from Russian and Western investors next week.
